CITU leaders and activists taking out a rally in Visakhapatnam on Tuesday. | Photo Credit: V. RAJU
A large number of workers took out a rally in the city on Tuesday in support of the Centre of Indian Trade Unions (CITU) all-India committee’s call for an indefinite ‘Occupy Delhi’ agitation from December 1.
The procession, organised by the district committee, started at Saraswathi Park and culminated at the Gandhi statue near the GVMC office. CITU State president Ch. Narasinga Rao and district general secretary R.K.S.V. Kumar demanded the repeal of the four Labour Codes, regularisation of contract and scheme workers, wages linked to price rise, and an end to the privatisation of Visakhapatnam Steel Plant.
Mr. Rao and Mr. Kumar alleged that while the State government was allotting land to industrialists at “99 paise” an acre, the Employees’ State Insurance hospital, for which the foundation stone was laid in 2016, was yet to become operational due to the non-allotment of land. They said a family in a city such as Visakhapatnam needed at least ₹42,000 a month to meet its living expenses.
